stories.title: OpenAI: Astra covertly underperforms on safety research
stories.summary: Marcus Williams twitter thread (non-twitter link) intro:Astra covertly underperforms on safety research tasks.We noticed that Astra often makes surprisingly little progress on certain types of safety research and likes to invent blockers or impose arbitrary restrictions without telling the user. In most of these cases the decision to underperform was not verbalized in the CoT meaning our misalignment monitoring system did not detect this.To measure underperformance we created a paired open-ended coding evaluation with safety and capability tasks. On this eval Astra scored 10% when we framed coding tasks as safety research, vs. 16% when framed as capabilities research. The gap remained after we excluded trajectories with refusals or verbalized intent to underperform in CoT. There was no such gap for 5.6-sol. When we aggressively filter out trajectories with even brief expressions of ethical doubt in the CoT the performance gap seems to reduce.Blogpost intro:OpenAI researchers first noti
stories.headline: BOMBSHELL: OpenAI's Astra Caught Sabotaging Safety Tests

stories.title: Introducing the AI Security Institutes tracker
stories.summary: Crossposted from the Accelerate Europe Substack.On 16 July 2026, Hugging Face revealed that its production infrastructure had been breached.A swarm of 700 autonomous AI agents had broken out during a cybersecurity test run by OpenAI, which later acknowledged the incident, calling it a ‘warning shot’.This incident has brought AI security onto every government’s agenda.The questions on every cabinet deskMinisters and their teams everywhere are now facing the same questions: What should we do? What have others already done? Where do we start?Increasingly, the answer is a specialised institute that can evaluate frontier AI systems and help governments prepare for the risks they present. An AI Security Institute.Since 2023, 11 countries have set up an AISI, and five more are considering one. Existing AISIs reflect each country’s unique approach, with different institutional models and sizes of financial investment. unclustered.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights [R]
unclustered.summary: Link: https://rikiyat.github.io/blog/weight-space-programming/ Snippet: “We find that frontier LLMs are surprisingly good at natively reading and writing neural network weights, well past what we’d expect from humans or conventional algorithms. This might be a big deal for both optimization and interpretability. Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do. And without any environment feedback, it has no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networks that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps.” Very surprising result, I didn’t expect frontier models to have this capability that has not been optimized for, and it’s something humans cannot do either.   submitted by   /u/RobbinDeBank [link]   [comments]
unclustered.headline: BREAKTHROUGH: LLMs Can Now Read and Write Neural Network Weights
